title: The Sixth Constable: The Magpie's Treasure
full_text:
The Sixth Constable related:

'A noble lady accused her faithful maidservant of stealing an emerald necklace, demanding her immediate imprisonment. The maid wept, swearing by her honor that she had never touched the jewel.

I noticed that the dressing-room window was open, overlooking a tall cedar tree where a tame magpie nested. Knowing the bird’s instinct for glittering objects, I sent a boy up the cedar tree to inspect the nest.

There, woven among the twigs and dry leaves, lay the emerald necklace, along with three silver spoons and a golden thimble!

The lady wept in remorse, embraced her innocent maid, gifted her a dowry, and praised the prudence that investigates before condemning.'
moral: Do not accuse an innocent servant of theft before searching all natural possibilities.
